items.front: In Amazon SQS, does receiving a message delete it from the queue?
items.back: No. It stays in the queue, hidden from other consumers.
items.extra: The consumer deletes the message after it finishes processing.

items.front: With Amazon SNS and Amazon SQS, several services must each get every message and keep it until processed. What do you build?
items.back: An SNS topic with one SQS queue per service.
items.extra: SNS delivers each message to all the subscribed queues; each queue keeps its own copy.

items.front: In Amazon SNS, does a standard topic keep messages for a subscriber that is offline?
items.back: No. SNS messages are not persisted.
items.extra: Subscribe an SQS queue to keep each copy until it is processed.

items.front: In Amazon SQS, can a standard queue deliver one message twice?
items.back: Yes. A standard queue delivers at least once.
items.extra: Design consumers to be idempotent, so a second copy does no harm.

items.front: In EC2 Auto Scaling, workers poll an SQS queue. Which metric should the group track?
items.back: Backlog per instance: visible messages divided by InService instances.
items.extra: Metric math: ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible divided by GroupInServiceInstances.

items.front: In Amazon EventBridge, does a Classic event bus keep its events?
items.back: No. To keep events, add an archive.
items.extra: Custom Event Bus - Classic is the bus type with rules and targets.

items.front: In Amazon SQS, a delay queue or the visibility timeout: which one hides a message as soon as it is added?
items.back: The delay queue.
items.extra: The visibility timeout hides a message after a consumer receives it.

items.front: In Amazon SQS, can you convert an existing standard queue to a FIFO queue?
items.back: No. Create a new FIFO queue.
items.extra: Choose the queue type when you create the queue.

items.front: In an SQS FIFO queue, do messages of different message groups keep their order?
items.back: No. Strict order holds inside one message group.
items.extra: Messages of different groups can arrive or be processed out of order.

items.front: In Amazon SQS, each customer's events must stay in order, and customers must run in parallel. What do you use?
items.back: A FIFO queue with the customer ID as message group ID.
items.extra: Different message groups are processed in parallel.

items.front: In an SQS FIFO queue, two messages have the same deduplication ID inside the 5 minute deduplication interval. How many copies are delivered?
items.back: One copy.
items.extra: SQS treats the second message as a duplicate.

items.front: In Amazon SQS, can a FIFO queue use a standard queue as its dead-letter queue?
items.back: No. Its dead-letter queue must also be a FIFO queue.
items.extra: The dead-letter queue of a standard queue is also a standard queue.

items.front: In Amazon SQS, can a dead-letter queue be in a different Region from its source queue?
items.back: No. It must be in the same account and Region.
items.extra: The source queue and its dead-letter queue share one AWS account and one Region.

items.front: In Amazon SQS, how long should a dead-letter queue keep messages?
items.back: Longer than the retention period of the source queue.
items.extra: In a standard queue, expiration counts from the original enqueue time.

items.front: In AWS Lambda with an SQS event source, how long should the queue's visibility timeout be?
items.back: At least six times the function timeout.
items.extra: This gives Lambda time to retry when the function is throttled.

items.front: In Amazon SNS, a topic delivers nothing to a subscribed SQS queue. What is missing?
items.back: A queue policy that allows the topic to send messages.
items.extra: The subscription alone does not give the topic permission.

items.front: In Amazon SNS, one subscriber needs only some of a topic's messages. What do you add?
items.back: A filter policy on that subscription.
items.extra: Without a filter policy, a subscriber receives every message.

items.front: In Amazon SNS, does a dead-letter queue attach to the topic or to a subscription?
items.back: To a subscription.
items.extra: SNS delivers messages at the subscription level.

items.front: In Amazon SQS, a role in another account has an IAM policy that allows sqs:SendMessage. Is that enough?
items.back: No. The queue's access policy must also allow the role.
items.extra: Identity-based policies alone are not sufficient for cross-account access.

items.front: In Amazon SQS, can you edit the key policy of the AWS managed KMS key for SQS?
items.back: No. You cannot modify that key policy.
items.extra: For SNS to deliver to a queue encrypted with AWS KMS, use a customer managed key whose policy allows SNS.

items.front: In Amazon SQS, short polling or long polling: which returns at once when the queue is empty?
items.back: Short polling.
items.extra: Long polling waits until a message arrives or the wait time ends.

items.front: In AWS, an app must react to EC2 instance state changes without polling. What do you use?
items.back: An EventBridge rule on the default event bus.
items.extra: The default event bus receives events from AWS services automatically.

items.front: In AWS Lambda with an SQS event source, how do you retry only the failed messages of a batch?
items.back: Return a partial batch response with ReportBatchItemFailures.
items.extra: Lambda then makes the failed messages visible again, not the successful ones.

items.front: In AWS, a task must run one time, three days from now. Which service schedules it?
items.back: EventBridge Scheduler, with a one-time schedule.
items.extra: SQS delay queues and message timers reach [up to 15 minutes in the future](../facts/sqs.md#sqs-eventbridge-scheduler-for-advanced-scheduling).

items.front: In Amazon SQS, a queue keeps a message for {{c1::4 days}} by default.
items.extra: A message that is older than the retention period is deleted unread.

items.front: In Amazon SQS, the longest message retention period is {{c1::14 days}}.
items.extra: The shortest retention period is [60 seconds](../facts/sqs.md#sqs-message-retention-range).

items.front: In Amazon SQS, the default visibility timeout is {{c1::30 seconds}}.
items.extra: A job that runs longer than the timeout lets a second consumer receive the same message.

items.front: In Amazon SQS, the longest visibility timeout is {{c1::12 hours}}.
items.extra: The limit counts from the ReceiveMessage request. Extending the timeout does not reset it.

items.front: In Amazon SQS, the longest wait time of one long-polling ReceiveMessage call is {{c1::20 seconds}}.
items.extra: Any wait time greater than zero turns on long polling.

items.front: In Amazon SQS, the longest delay of a delay queue is {{c1::15 minutes}}.
items.extra: For a later start, AWS recommends EventBridge Scheduler.

items.front: In an SQS FIFO queue, the default throughput without batching is {{c1::300 messages per second}}.
items.extra: The default rises to [3,000 messages per second with batching](../facts/sqs.md#sqs-faq-fifo-default-throughput-3000-with-batching-300-without). High throughput mode allows more.

items.front: In Amazon EventBridge, the maximum number of targets of one rule is {{c1::5}}.
items.extra: The quota is not adjustable. More receivers need a second rule or an SNS topic as a target.
